title: Sugar Research and Development Services (Consequential Amendments—Excise) Bill 2013

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would broaden the sugar cane research levy and increase its rate as part of reforms funding an industry-owned research and development body.
The levy would rise from 14 to 70 cents per tonne, with producers and processors each responsible for half and regulations unable to change that split.
The changes would start on 1 July 2013 and cover sugar cane stalks, including stalks with leaves, while excluding leaves purchased or processed alone.
changes: Sugar cane sales would be treated as occurring when the first payment was made.
The levy would also cover cane grown and processed by the same establishment, or processed for an owner under contract.
The maximum levy rate would be removed, allowing regulations to set higher or lower rates.
Obsolete provisions for the former retail-packaged sugar levy would be repealed.
summary.affected: Sugar cane growers, producers and processing businesses liable for the levy are affected.

speeches.speaker: John Cobb
speeches.brief: Supported the Sugar Research and Development Services bills as a reform backed by most of the industry, under which Sugar Research Australia would replace separate research bodies and receive a 70c per tonne levy paid equally by growers and mills, while raising concerns about consultation, regional research, conflicts of interest and the legislation's rushed 1 July 2013 commencement.

speeches.speaker: George Christensen
speeches.brief: Supported the Sugar Research and Development Services bills, saying they would consolidate research functions in Sugar Research Australia, reduce duplication and secure funding through a 70c per tonne levy, while urging swift passage to provide certainty for research staff and the industry's future.

acts.title: Sugar Research and Development Services (Consequential Amendments—Excise) Act 2013
